chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Abbas ibn Al-Walid, from Al-Walid ibn Sabih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who married a free woman, so he found her to be a slave who had concealed herself to him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If she had married him from without her master, so the marriage is invalidated.' I said, 'So how would the dower be dealt with, which she had taken from him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he can find anything from what he had given her, so let him take it, and if he does not find anything, so there is nothing for him upon her; and if it was such that her master had married her to him, he would have recourse to her master with what was taken from him, and for her master, upon him, would be a tenth of her price if she was a virgin, and if she was not a virgin, so it would be half of the tenth of her price due to what she has permitted from her private parts.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And she would observe the waiting period of the slave girl.' I said, 'Supposing she were to come with a child?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Her children from him are free ones, when the marriage was without the permission of the master.'

key_terms.عِدَّةَ الْأَمَةِ: The waiting period of the slave girl

ai.seo_question: What are the fiqh rulings when a man marries a free woman who is actually a slave?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the fiqh of 'gharar' (uncertainty) in marriage contracts, specifically addressing the scenario where a slave woman conceals her status from a free man. It distinguishes between the validity of the marriage depending on whether the matchmaker was from her masters or not, and details the financial restitution of the dower and compensation to the masters based on virginity. Furthermore, it establishes that offspring from this union are free, reflecting the Shia principle that the child's status follows the father unless specified otherwise, while the woman observes the waiting period of a slave.
